sources.title: ASSE International Plumbing Dictionary, 6th Edition
sources.license: free public PDF; copyright ASSE International
sources.notes: Trade dictionary used for fixture-level vocabulary that the model codes define only in passing.

sources.title: 40 CFR 141.2 - National Primary Drinking Water Regulations definitions
sources.notes: Potable-water definitions used to pin down supply-water terms the plumbing code assumes.

sources.title: International Plumbing Code 2021 (Chapters 1-10)
sources.license: proprietary model code; free read-only access, no redistribution
sources.notes: Read through the Texas 2021 IPC adoption on UpCodes, plus the 2020 Plumbing Code of New York State PDF, which adopts the 2018 IPC with amendments. Definitions are paraphrased; no code text is stored in this repo.

sources.title: 29 CFR 1910.146 - Permit-Required Confined Spaces
sources.publisher: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration
sources.notes: Confined-space entry requirements that apply to pits, vaults, and tanks.

sources.title: 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P - Excavations
sources.publisher: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration
sources.notes: Trenching and excavation safety for underground plumbing work.

sources.title: Cross-Connection Control Manual (EPA 816-R-03-002)
sources.publisher: US Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Water
sources.notes: Backflow and cross-connection device taxonomy; the glossary is on p.48 of the PDF.

sources.title: WaterSense product criteria (toilets, faucets, showerheads, urinals)
sources.notes: Current flow-rate and flush-volume criteria for water-efficient fixtures.

sources.title: Uniform Plumbing Code 2024 (IAPMO/ANSI UPC 1-2024)
sources.publisher: International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials (IAPMO)
sources.license: proprietary model code; free read-only edition
sources.notes: Read from IAPMO's free read-only edition and cross-checked against the 2022 California Plumbing Code, which adopts the 2021 UPC.
